subject: Civil Engineering
title: Bridge Collapses Through History
description: A fast breakdown of Bridge Collapses Through History for builders.

hook.text: More bridges have collapsed from floods than any other cause. Water wins most fights.

buildup.text: Scour washes away the soil under piers. Without foundation, the bridge tips over.

discovery.text: Overloading is the second biggest cause — trucks heavier than the design limit.

twist.text: Many collapses happen to bridges already flagged as 'structurally deficient.'

climax.text: The U.S. has over 42,000 structurally deficient bridges still carrying traffic.

punchline.text: Most bridges don't fail suddenly — they fail from neglect.

quiz.question: What is the leading cause of bridge collapses worldwide?

details.summary: Bridge collapses have occurred throughout history from causes including overloading, design errors, material fatigue, scour, and environmental forces. Each major collapse from the Tay Bridge in 1879 to the Morandi Bridge in 2018 has driven improvements in engineering knowledge, materials.
details.whyItMatters: Every bridge collapse teaches lessons that prevent future failures. The engineering profession's systematic study of failures has made modern bridges far safer than historical ones.
takeaways: Scour, the erosion of soil around foundations, is the leading cause of failure
Fatigue cracking from repeated loading causes gradual hidden deterioration
Each major collapse has led to specific code changes and inspection reforms

faq.question: What is the most common cause of bridge collapse worldwide?
faq.answer: Hydraulic scour, where flowing water erodes soil around bridge foundations, causes more bridge collapses than any other factor. Floods accelerate scour, undermining piers that then tilt or sink. The I-90 Schoharie Creek Bridge collapse in 1987 and many others resulted from scour during flood events.

faq.question: What lessons came from the 2018 Morandi Bridge collapse in Genoa?
faq.answer: The Morandi Bridge collapse killed 43 people and revealed that Italy had thousands of aging bridges with inadequate inspection. It accelerated bridge monitoring programs across Europe and raised questions about the long-term durability of prestressed concrete bridge cables exposed to marine.
